questions.question: Points P and S are two points lying on the same side of line segment QR such that M is the mid-point of both the line segments PR and SQ. Then,
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Since **M** is the mid-point of both line segments **PR** and **SQ**, the diagonals of the quadrilateral **PQRS** bisect each other at **M**.

A quadrilateral whose diagonals bisect each other is always a **parallelogram**. Therefore, **PQRS** is a parallelogram.

In a parallelogram, opposite sides are parallel, so **PQ || SR**.

With **PR** acting as a transversal line, the alternate interior angles must be equal:

⇒ ∠QPR = ∠SRP

Since **M** lies on the line segment **PR**, this can be written as:

⇒ ∠QPM = ∠SRM

**∴ The correct answer is ∠QPM = ∠SRM.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

⇒ **M** is the mid-point of **PR** ⇒ **PM = MR**

⇒ **M** is the mid-point of **SQ** ⇒ **QM = SM**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/d662a677fbb08af709763d1b09542bd67e7f7ffda64db79aaf7ac64b43a14917.png] 

Now, consider triangles **ΔPQM** and **ΔRSM**:

⇒ **PM = RM** (Since **M** is the mid-point of **PR**)

⇒ **QM = SM** (Since **M** is the mid-point of **SQ**)

⇒ **∠PMQ = ∠RMS** (Vertically opposite angles)

Therefore, by the **SAS (Side-Angle-Side) congruence criterion**:

⇒ **ΔPQM ≅ ΔRSM**

By **CPCT (Corresponding Parts of Congruent Triangles)**, the corresponding angles of congruent triangles are equal:

⇒ **∠QPM = ∠SRM**

**Analysis of other options:**

⇒ **Option (1) ∠QPM = ∠RSM:** Incorrect, as these are not corresponding angles under the congruence relation.

⇒ **Option (3) ∠RSM = ∠SRM:** Incorrect, as this would require **SM = RM**, which is only true if the diagonals are equal (i.e., a rectangle).

⇒ **Option (4) ∠QPM = ∠PQM:** Incorrect, as this would require **PM = QM**, which is not true in a general parallelogram.

**∴ The correct answer is ∠QPM = ∠SRM.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Parallelogram Diagonal Theorem

A quadrilateral is a parallelogram if and only if its diagonals bisect each other.

SAS Congruence Rule

If two sides and the included angle of one triangle are equal to two sides and the included angle of another triangle, then the two triangles are congruent.

Alternate Interior Angles

When two parallel lines are cut by a transversal, the alternate interior angles formed are equal.</p

questions.question: The pressure inside two soap bubbles is found to be 1.01 atm and 1.02 atm. Assuming that both the bubbles have the same surface tension, what will be the ratio of their volume in the air?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is option 3) i.e. 8 : 1

 

__CONCEPT__:

__
 
• Excess pressure inside a soap bubble: 

 
 
• ​Consider a spherical soap bubble with radius R.
 
 

​ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f752efa7a4e2f509b4261a47bd09debbcf70cebfb023b152ebbdb905390ddf2b.png] 

 
• A soap bubble has two free surfaces - towards the inside and outside. Due to surface tension, the molecules on the surface will experience a net force towards the inside, normal to the surface. Hence, there is excess pressure inside than outside.
 
• Let Pi be the pressure inside the bubble and Po be the pressure outside the bubble. Excess pressure, P = Pi - Po
 
• Due to the excess pressure inside, the soap bubble will have a tendency to expand by force acting outwards.
 
• Let the expansion of the soap bubble in terms of displacement be dR. 

Work done by excess pressure = force × displacement = pressure × surface area × dR = P × 4πR2 × dR ----(1)

 
• Let the surface tension be T. Surface tension = force per unit length = energy per unit area.

Energy (work done) = T × area = 2T × change in area = 2T × (4π{R+dR}2 - 4πR2) = 2T (4π(2RdR)) ----(2)

Equating (1) and (2),

P × 4πR2 × dR = 2T × (4π(2RdR)) 

Excess pressure, P=(4T)/(R)

CALCULATION__:

Given that:

Pressure inside, Pᵢ' = 1.01 atm Pᵢ'' = 1.02 atm

The atmospheric pressure will be the pressure outside the bubble, Pₒ = 1 atm

Excess pressure, P = P_i - P_o = (4T)/(R)

Let P' and P'' be the excess pressure of the two bubbles.

P' = Pi' - Po = 1.01 atm - 1 atm = 0.01 atm

P'' = Pi'' - Po = 1.02 atm - 1 atm = 0.02 atm

Since the surface tension T is the same for both the bubbles, excess pressure P∝(1)/(R)

Let R' and R" be the radii of the two soap bubbles.

∴ The **ratio of excess pressure** (P')/(P") = (0.01)/(0.02) = (R")/(R') ----(1)

The volume of a spherical soap bubble is given by V =(4)/(3)pi R³

**⇒ V ∝ R³ **

Let V' and V'' be the volume of the two soap bubbles.

Ratio (V')/(V") = ((R')/(R"))³ ----(2)

Substituting (1) in (2),

(V')/(V") = ((0.02)/(0.01))³ = (8)/(1)

questions.solution:
**__LOAD__****:**

__
 
• The **load (ld)** instruction loads **from memory using a segment or flat address expression** and places the result into one or more registers.
 
• It is an ordinary non-synchronizing memory instruction (see Memory Model).
 
• There are four variants of the ld instruction, depending on the number of destinations: one, two, three, or four. The size of the value loaded is specified by the instruction's compound type.
 
• The value is stored in the destination register following the rules in Operands. Integer values are sign-extended or zero-extended to fit the destination register size.

**FETCH__****:**

__
 
• The Program Counter (PC) starts at 0000. This means that the first address in RAM where the computer will look for instruction is 0000.
 
• The computer needs somewhere to store the current address in RAM that it is looking for. This is what the Memory Address Register (MAR) is for. 0000 is therefore copied into the MAR.
 
• A signal is now sent down through the Address bus to the RAM.
 
• The Control Unit sends out a memory read signal, and the contents of the address 0000 are copied through the data bus to the Memory Data Register.
 
• As the **data fetched** during the fetch stage is an instruction, it is copied into the Instruction Register (IR).
 
• As the first instruction has been fetched, the system is at the end of the **Fetch stage of the cycle**.
 
• The program counter can be incremented by 1, so the system is ready to read the next instruction when the next Fetch cycle starts.

 

**LOOP__****:**

__
 
• The LOOP instruction is mainly used to simulate the different loops in HLL. The Loop instructions use the CX register to indicate the loop count.
 
• The Loop instruction decrements CX without changing any flags.
 
• If CX is not zero after the decrement, control is transferred to the destination label.
 
• The jump is a SHORT jump only.
 
• The syntax of the Loop instruction is: **LOOP label**

**​

JUMP__:**

 
• The jump instruction transfers the program sequence to the memory address given in the operand based on the specified flag.
 
• Jump instructions are 2 types: Unconditional Jump Instructions and Conditional Jump Instructions.

questions.question: If (201)₈ = (81)ₓ, where 8 and x represent the base of the respective number systems, then what will be the value of x?

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The **octal ****numeral system **is a positional numeral system that represents numbers using a radix/base of 8.

 
 
• ​It uses numbers from 0 to 7.
 
• It requires only 3 bits to represent value of any digit.
 
• It is used in computers and digital numbering systems.
 
 
 
• The **hexadecimal numeral system** is a positional numeral system that represents numbers using a radix/base of 16.
 
 
• It uses 16 distinct symbols. "0"–"9" represent values 0 to 9, and "A"–"F" represent values from 10 to 15.
 
• Each hexadecimal digit represents four bits (binary digits). An 8-bit byte can be conveniently represented from 00 to FF in hexadecimal.
 
• Hex codes are used in many areas of computing to simplify binary codes.
 
 
 
• Conversion of the** octal number to hexadecimal requires two steps- converting octal numbers to decimal numbers and then converting decimal numbers to hexadecimal numbers**.
 
• Let's convert octal 201 into hexadecimal and see if our selected option is correct -
 
 
• Multiply each digit of the octal number by the corresponding power of eight.
 
• 2x8² + 0x8¹ + 1x8⁰
 
• 128 + 0 + 1 = 129
 
• Now, our next step is to convert decimal 129 into hexadecimal
 
• Divide (129)₁₀ successively by 16 until the quotient is 0
 
• 129/16 = 8, remainder is 1
 
• 8/16 = 0, remainder is 8
 
• Read from the remainders from the bottom
 
• We find 81.
 
 
 
• Hence, **x represents 16, i.e. hexadecimal system**.

questions.question: The minimum change in the measured variable which produces an effective response of the instrument is known as
questions.solution:
The minimum change in the measured variable which produces an effective response of the instrument is known as **resolution.**

__Concept:__

The static performance parameters of the instruments are:

 
• Accuracy
 
• Precision
 
• Resolution
 
• Threshold
 
• Static sensitivity
 
• Linearity
 
• Hysteresis
 
• Backlash
 
• Dead band
 
• Drift

 

 
• Accuracy: It is the closeness with which an instrument reading approaches the true value of the quantity being measured. It means conformity to truth.
 
• Precision: It is defined as the ability of the instrument to reproduce a certain set of readings within a given accuracy
 
• **Drift:** It is defined as the variation of output for a given input caused due to change in the sensitivity of the instrument to certain interfering input like temperature changes, component instability, etc.
 
• Resolution: It is defined as the smallest increment in the measured value that can be detected with certainty by the instrument.
 
• Threshold: It is defined as the minimum value of input below which no output can be detected.
 
• Static sensitivity: It is defined as the ratio of the magnitude of response to the magnitude of the quantity being measured.
 
• Linearity: It represents the output of the instrument which is a linear function of the input.
 
• Hysteresis: It is defined as the magnitude of error caused in the output for a given value of input when this value is approached from opposite directions, i.e. from ascending order and then descending order.
 
• Dead band: It is defined as the largest change of the measurand to which the instrument does not respond.
 
• Backlash: It is defined as the maximum distance or angle through which any part of the mechanical system may be moved in one direction without causing motion of the next part.

• According to Biot-Savart’s law, the magnitude of the magnetic field dB is proportional to the current I, the element length |dl|, and inversely proportional to the square of the distance r. Its direction is perpendicular to the plane containing dl and r.
 
• Thus, in vector notation,dB = (mu₀i ~dl times r)/(4pi r³)
